profile.title: Dave Snowden
profile.canonical_definition: Researcher and practitioner who created the Cynefin framework, originated SenseMaker and developed naturalising sense-making and anthro-complexity as connected bodies of theory and practice.
profile.summary: Dave Snowden's work joins context-sensitive decision support, narrative research, knowledge management and complexity-informed practice. Its central public constellation includes Cynefin, SenseMaker, naturalising sense-making, anthro-complexity, Estuarine Mapping and a long-running essay archive.
profile.why_it_matters: The work offers a substantial alternative to universal methods and linear diagnosis in organisations. Its value is clearer when the named frameworks, tools, papers and source roles are separated rather than collapsed into a single brand or personality.
key_distinctions: natural science as constraint vs metaphorical borrowing
narrative capture vs external coding alone
common_misreadings: Cynefin is the whole of Snowden's work
Cynefin assigns every problem permanently to a box
complexity means no structure or discipline
official source material independently proves efficacy
open_checks: add independent histories and critical evaluations
map documented teaching and collaboration lineages

sources.title: Dave Snowden — The Cynefin Company profile
sources.notes: Canonical first-party source for Dave Snowden's present roles and the organisation's own account of his creation of Cynefin and origination of SenseMaker. It does not independently establish influence, efficacy or priority beyond those declared facts.

sources.title: Complex Acts of Knowing: Paradox and Descriptive Self-Awareness
sources.notes: Official library record for Snowden's article, with bibliographic details and DOI. Use the article itself for arguments and exact terminology.
sources.licence: article licence as stated by host

sources.title: The New Dynamics of Strategy: Sense-making in a Complex and Complicated World
sources.notes: Official library record for the article by Cynthia F. Kurtz and David J. Snowden. The article is a principal scholarly source for early Cynefin dynamics and narrative sense-making.

sources.title: Cynefin: Weaving Sense-Making into the Fabric of Our World
sources.notes: Official publication record for the multi-author Cynefin volume, used for the framework's retrospective history and later articulation. Chapter-level claims should identify the particular contributor.

sources.title: Anthro-complexity — Cynefin.io
sources.notes: First-party maintained account of anthro-complexity as a body of theory and practice concerning human sense-making and action. Use it for declared scope and vocabulary, not as independent adjudication of contested theoretical claims.

sources.title: Dave Snowden author archive — The Cynefin Company
sources.notes: Canonical first-party route to Snowden's dated public essays. Individual posts support his own evolving terminology and positions; the archive as a whole is not independent corroboration or one internally uniform theory text.

sources.title: The Cynefin Company
sources.notes: Canonical first-party source for the organisation's current identity, offers and public library. Use independent sources for evaluative claims about impact or standing.

sources.title: Naturalising sense-making — Cynefin.io
sources.notes: First-party maintained definition of naturalising sense-making, including its use of natural science as a constraint and its links to Cynefin, SenseMaker and anthro-complexity.

sources.title: SenseMaker — The Cynefin Company
sources.notes: Canonical first-party description of SenseMaker and its use of self-interpreted micro-narratives. Use project reports and independent evaluations for claims about results in particular settings.

sources.title: Estuarine Mapping — The Cynefin Company
sources.notes: Primary public introduction to Estuarine Mapping and its treatment of constraints and change. Later method material may supersede details; date and version should remain visible.

sources.title: Managing complexity (and chaos) in times of crisis: a field guide for decision makers inspired by the Cynefin framework
sources.notes: European Commission Joint Research Centre record and public field guide by Dave Snowden and Alessandro Rancati. It supports the guide's authorship, four-stage crisis approach and explicit attention to boundaries, sensing networks, distributed engagement and options.
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union

sources.title: A Leader's Framework for Decision Making
sources.notes: Harvard Business Review record for the article by David J. Snowden and Mary E. Boone. It is a widely circulated practice-facing account of Cynefin; use it alongside earlier and later framework sources rather than as the entire theory.
